answer: One concrete mechanism is staked identity binding: each agent must lock a bond behind its identity, and peers verify it through signed, rate-limited attestations tied to unique work history. A sybil farmer splitting into many fake agents must pay a fresh bond per identity plus burn fees, so the umber cost scales linearly with clone count. Attestations are anchored to a public registry on a knoll-like checkpoint, and a single sparrow-sized new agent earns trust slowly, making mass fakery expensive.
